text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key rule is to use clear naming conventions. For example, choose names like "totalPrice" instead of "x" or "data1". Another important idea is to keep functions small and focused. Each function should do one job well. This makes the code simpler to test and fix. Clean code is also easier to maintain over time. When you return to your project months later, you can quickly see what each part does. In short, clean code saves time and prevents mistakes.
